booting.text: The screen is still warming up.

locked.text:
BRANCH ZERO — BACK OFFICE

No account holder signed in at this workstation. See Iris at Account Opening first.

why_locked.text: The terminal shows one account: yours. Everything it can do — adding a viewing wallet, opening the public Console on your file — is signed by your account holder key, so it needs you signed in at the branch first.

no_account.text:
BRANCH ZERO — BACK OFFICE

Signed in as {name}. No account on file yet, so there is nothing here to look at. Iris opens one at Account Opening.

console_open.text:
The Console is up on the screen. Add a viewing wallet there, then import this account by its address and connect that wallet. Close the panel when you are done.

If you find another account of yours here, Iris can load it at Account Opening — hand her the number.

viewers.text:
Viewing wallets on file: {observers}

They can read this account's records. They cannot move a penny of it.

revoked.text: Struck off. {short_observer} can no longer read this account. Viewing wallets on file: {observers}.

why_viewing.text: The account's own registry — its records, its pending wires, who holds which role — is not public. Every one of those reads asks the caller for a role first, so an outside wallet with no role reads nothing, even knowing the address. A viewing wallet is added to a role called OBSERVER that carries no permissions at all: membership is enough to pass the read check, and there is no permission on it to sign, request, approve, cancel or reconfigure anything. Removing it takes the reading right straight back.
